claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training.

Could you tell me, is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or similar full-time courses)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex is 18 and not currently in approved education or training, there are a couple of scenarios that could still allow you to claim Child Benefit:

1. If Alex is 16 or 17 years old and has left education or training and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks. However, since Alex is 18, this wouldn't apply.

2. There are also some circumstances that would stop Child Benefit eligibility, such as if Alex has started paid work for 24 hours or more a week, started an apprenticeship in England, or is receiving certain benefits like Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Could you tell me:
- Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week?
- Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all right now, and he's not receiving any benefits in his own right either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, the situation for Alex doesn't look favourable for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me explain:

- Alex is 18 years old
- He is not in approved education or training
- He is not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (and even if he were, this provision only applies to 16 or 17 year olds)

For children aged 16 or over, you can normally only continue to receive Child Benefit if they remain in approved education or training until they turn 20.

Just to confirm before I make a final determination: has Alex recently left education or training and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services? Or are there any other circumstances about Alex's situation that you think might be relevant?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He just finished school and is at home at the moment. That's all there is to it really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to make a determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Alex is 18 years old** and has finished school
- **He is not in approved education or training** – For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can normally only continue if the child remains in approved education or training until they turn 20
- **The careers service/armed forces exception doesn't apply** – The provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks when a young person registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services only applies to 16 or 17 year olds, not to 18 year olds

**However**, if Alex's circumstances change in the future – for example, if he enrols in an approved education or training course before he turns 20 – you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for him at that point. If that happens, you would need to make a new claim.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. Is there anything else I can help you with?
